# The Stars That Tell Time

## Scripture
"He determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name." - Psalm 147:4

## Reflection
Tonight, step outside and look up. The stars appear fixed, eternal—but they are actually in constant, measurable motion. Astronomers call it "proper motion"—the slow drift of stars across the sky over thousands of years. Barnard's Star, for instance, crawls across the celestial sphere at a seemingly glacial pace, yet it's moving faster than any other star visible to the naked eye.

We live in a world obsessed with speed. We want immediate answers, instant growth, rapid healing. But God works on a different timescale. He who numbered the stars and calls them each by name is not hurried by our calendars. The same God who set these celestial bodies in their ancient paths is patiently at work in your life—moving, shaping, guiding, even when you cannot perceive the progress.

The stars don't rush. They simply remain faithful to their Creator's design, trusting His timing. Like them, we are held by the same steady hand. The slow drift of a distant star is not aimless wandering—it is obedience to divine physics. Your slow seasons are not wasted years; they are orbits of purpose under the watchful eye of the One who knows your name.

## Prayer
Patient Creator, teach us to trust Your timing. When we grow restless in our waiting, remind us that You who guide the stars also guide our steps. Help us find peace in the slow work of Your hands, knowing that nothing in our lives drifts beyond Your care. In Jesus' name, Amen.
